Hi Todd,

Thanks for the detailed note. Bolts and BCH payouts come from two different settings, so getting Bolts doesn't prove your BCH is going to the right place.

Bolts are tied to your pool account, the one you log into at pool.harlolabs.com with your BCH wallet linked. Your share of a block goes to whatever is in the Worker field of your miner's pool settings. Harlo Pool expects that field to be your Bitcoin Cash wallet address, with "x" as the password. If the Worker field has a name, a nickname or a Bitcoin (BTC) address instead, your spins and Bolts still work, but your mining rewards aren't going to your BCH wallet.

Here is what to check, in this order:

1. Open your miner's web page and go to the pool settings. Make sure the stratum URL is stratum+tcp://pool.harlolabs.com:8888 and the Worker field holds only your BCH address. It usually starts with "bitcoincash:q" or just "q".
2. Check that this is exactly the same address as the wallet you're watching. If you've ever used more than one wallet app, the miner may be pointed at the other one.
3. Paste that address into any public Bitcoin Cash block explorer. The explorer shows everything sent to the address, even if your wallet app hasn't synced or hides it.
4. Keep in mind that freshly mined BCH can't be spent until 100 more blocks have been found, which takes about 17 hours. If the pool pays straight from the block reward, the coins can take that long to show up.

Also, when someone else finds the block, half the reward is split among everyone mining based on recent work. With a small miner, your share of each block can be a very small amount.

I can't see your pool account or the payout records for those two blocks, so I've passed your case to JD, our hardware lead. He can check where your share went. The team is back tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come to you by email. If you'd like an answer sooner, the Harlo community is very active on Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, and you can mention @nullhashrate there to reach JD directly.

If step 1 shows the wrong address in the Worker field, just correct it and save. Future rewards will then go to your wallet.

Best regards,
Hal

Hi Todd,

Thanks for the screenshot. Your pool settings are correct. The host is pool.harlolabs.com on port 8888 with Stratum V1, and Pool 1 is getting 100% of the hashrate. The W. field has your Bitcoin Cash address followed by ".asic1". That address.name format is the standard way to label a miner, so nothing needs to change on the miner.

The ".asic1" may be why the blockchain search found nothing. It's only a label for your miner and isn't part of the wallet address, so an explorer won't recognise it. Search again with just ····. If that still shows nothing, also try it without the "bitcoincash:" prefix.

Hi Todd,

You're right, and I'm sorry. You asked a clear question and waited a week with no answer while two more blocks were found. That shouldn't have happened.

I re-checked your settings from the screenshot. Your miner is pointed at pool.harlolabs.com on port 8888 using Stratum V1, Pool 1 gets 100% of the hashrate, and the worker is your Bitcoin Cash address with ".asic1" added as the miner's label. All of that is correct, and your Bolts working confirms the pool knows who you are. So this isn't a setup problem on your end. After four blocks with nothing showing on the blockchain, the question is what the pool has credited to you and when it pays out. I can't see the pool's payout records, so I can't answer that myself.

I've raised it again with the team today, marked as overdue and with all your details attached. A colleague will look up your pool balance and payout history and answer you in this thread. While you wait, log in at pool.harlolabs.com and check your account page. If it shows a balance or a payout history, reply with a screenshot. That will speed things up.

If you'd also like to ask the people who run the pool directly, the Harlo Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is very active. Mention @nullhashrate there to reach JD, our hardware lead.

Best regards,
Hal
